name: adaptive step search: find the largest k such that a monotone predicate holds at k, by a linear scan to 4, exponential probing, then binary search

sources.ref: hypothesis 6.165.10 (Techne lock; shrinker.py sha256 f364cbff...) hypothesis/internal/conjecture/junkdrawer.py find_integer (linear 1..4; lo=4, hi=5 doubling while f(hi); binary search to lo+1==hi; f(0) assumed true)

hypothesis 6.165.10 (Techne lock; shrinker.py sha256 f364cbff...) hypothesis/internal/conjecture/call sites: shrinker.py _node_program (repeat count and leftward offset), lower_common_node_offset, redistribute_numeric_pairs, lower_integers_together; shrinking/integer.py shift_right / mask_high_bits / shrink_by_multiples; ordering.py sort_regions; collection.py delete_k

questions.ancestry: One def in the pinned bytes; located by the name the flow gave (every adaptive loop calls it). Origin INHERITED, and the boundary is the def -- Nyx notes this as a case where the programmer's boundary looks correct (ruling: a low inherited rate is not the goal).
questions.mechanism: Try k = 1..4; if any fails return the last success. Otherwise double hi from 5 until f(hi) fails, then binary search between the last success and the first failure. Returns lo with f(lo) true and f(lo+1) false. Turns O(k) successive successes into O(log k) evaluations when the predicate is monotone in k.
questions.input: a predicate f: int -> bool, monotone (true up to some k*, false after), with f(0) assumed true
questions.output: an integer lo; f(lo) is true and f(lo+1) is false (if monotone; otherwise some local boundary)
questions.assumptions: monotonicity of f in k; that small answers are common (hence the linear scan first, stated in the comment); that f is cheap enough that doubling overshoot is acceptable
questions.fitness_value: MEASURED (standalone; nyx/specimens/hypothesis_shrinker/ablations/RECEIPT_N1_2026-09-11.json P-a4, N-e): find_integer(k <= 37) returned 37 in 12 predicate calls (linear scan would take 38); on the non-monotone f (true at 1-3 and 5-6) it returned 3 in 4 calls -- the local boundary, as the contract says, not the global one.
questions.failure_landscape: (a) non-monotone f: returns some boundary, not the largest k; every caller silently assumes monotonicity; (b) an f that is expensive and true for large k costs a doubling overshoot; (c) f(0) is never checked, so a caller whose base case fails gets a wrong answer.
questions.ablation: unknown -- designed: replace by a linear scan. Prediction: identical results, evaluations grow from O(log k) to O(k) on runs of deletable elements. Cheap to run standalone (P-a family) -- scheduled in ablations/.
questions.decomposability: linear probe / exponential probe / binary search -- three textbook pieces; the composition (linear first) is the only design decision.
questions.composability: Any 'how many of these can I do at once' loop; Proteus's enumerator does not need it, but any Prometheus organism that deletes or repeats adaptively could host it verbatim. Ancestor-free: it imports nothing.
questions.human_prior: That the answer is usually small (linear scan to 4 first). Stated in the comment as a cost argument.
questions.control: RUN: positive 37/12 calls; negative returns the first boundary (3) on a non-monotone predicate. Ref nyx/specimens/hypothesis_shrinker/ablations/RECEIPT_N1_2026-09-11.json.
questions.cheat: Counting the returned k as 'progress made' when f was non-monotone; control: assert f(lo) and not f(lo+1) after the call.
